copyright: North Window, Arches National Park, Moab, Utah, USA (© lightphoto/Getty Images)
description: Just north of Moab, Utah, Arches National Park is home to more than 2,000 natural sandstone arches – the densest concentration of arches in the world. Today's image, North Window, is one of the best-known formations in the park's Windows Section, where towering fins, openings and sculpted sandstone create a landscape that looks almost architectural.

copyright: A field of poppies (© lloyd-horgan/Getty Images)
description: For Remembrance Day, we are looking out over a field of poppies, recognised as symbols of remembrance for more than a century.

copyright: Aerial view of Rose Island, The Bahamas (© Abstract Aerial Art/Getty Images)
description: From above, Rose Island looks like a brushstroke of green surrounded by every shade of blue. Just five kilometres east of Paradise Island in The Bahamas, this slender cay trades busy roads and city blocks for sandy shores, shallow waters and an inland lagoon. Its peaceful appearance comes with a touch of movie drama. Rose Island was used as a filming location for the 1965 James Bond adventure Thunderball, including the explosive destruction of the Disco Volante.

copyright: Historic district of Triana, Seville, Spain (© Andrzej Rostek/Getty Images)
description: Cross the Guadalquivir River in Seville, the capital of Spain's Andalusia region, and the city's rhythm seems to change. On the other side lies Triana, a colourful neighbourhood where ceramics, flamenco and local traditions are woven into everyday life. Since the 19th century, the Isabel II Bridge, also known as the Triana Bridge, has connected the neighbourhood to Seville's historic centre.

copyright: Lanterns for Diwali in Mumbai, Maharashtra, India (© Dinodia Photo/Getty Images)
description: What happens when the darkest night of the year gets the brightest celebration? Diwali. The Festival of Lights is celebrated by millions worldwide, bringing together diyas, lanterns, rangoli, prayers, sweets and family gatherings.

copyright: A bison in the grasslands of Theodore Roosevelt National Park, North Dakota, USA (© Tandem Stock/Adobe Stock)
description: Bison are among the largest land mammals in the world, capable of weighing up to 900 kilograms and reaching speeds of 65 kilometres per hour despite their massive size. Despite often being called a buffalo, the American bison is not one of the true buffaloes, which are native to Africa and Asia. Its scientific name, Bison bison, leaves little room for confusion.

copyright: Bamboo forest, Pīpīwai Trail, Haleakalā National Park, Maui, Hawaii, USA (© MNStudio/Getty Images)
description: A volcano, a rainforest and a bamboo grove? Haleakalā National Park on Maui has all three. Spanning Maui from its 3,055-metre summit to the coast, the park protects landscapes that change dramatically with elevation, rainfall and temperature. It was established in 1916 as part of Hawaii National Park and became its own national park in 1961. The name Haleakalā translates to 'House of the Sun', reflecting the Hawaiian mo'olelo of Māui capturing the Sun to lengthen the day.
